newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee recovers from lows after selling bout.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee recovers from lows after selling bout.

text.p: London's January robusta coffee contract bore the brunt of a fierce bout of selling on Friday afternoon, widening the nearby spread in the absence of interest in spot November, traders said. Fresh fund and follow-through selling pounded January during the latter part of the session, triggering sell stops at around $1,415 and $1,400.
Vietnam was cited as a major seller and some residual sales were also noted from Indonesia.
But values recovered towards the close, with the nearby positions ending above the intraday lows.
January closed under psychological support at $1,400, $27 lower at $1,397, after sliding to $1,380.November finished $14 lower at $1,507 and overall volume totalled 5,430 lots.

"January has now broken out of the tight range but there is no selling on November and that is strengthening the switch," one trader said, adding that the Nov/Jan switch might well have seen its high for the meantime.
Traders said the London market seemed to have ignored all bullish news and had traded on technical indicators.
"The open interest has a large amount of funds so this market is purely technically driven," the trader said.
Other traders said a certain amount of bullish news was already factored into the market, which would account for the lack of reaction to recent developments in key producers Costa Rica and Colombia.
Costa Rica's ICAFE coffee institute said the 1996/97 crop could suffer further losses after torrential rains from Hurricane Lili flooded one coffee zone this week.
Five percent of the country's crop was wiped out after Hurricane Cesar swept through Central America in mid-August.
A truck drivers' strike entered its fourth day in Colombia, where a government minister was threatening to outlaw the action.
